name: Electric Motorcycle
description: A motorcycle powered by an electric motor of more than 750 watts, or able to go faster than 20 mph on its motor alone; this is where an electric two-wheeler past the e-bike limits lands, such as a Sur-Ron ridden on the road. Defined by Utah Code §41-6a-102 and regulated by §41-6a-1511, both from H.B. 381 (2026), effective May 6, 2026.
restrictions: A seat or saddle and no more than three wheels, with an electric motor of more than 750 watts or able to exceed 20 mph on motor power alone
Not an electric assisted bicycle or a motor assisted scooter
Has the rights and duties of a motorcycle operator under the traffic code
Riders need a driver's license with a motorcycle endorsement
Riders under 21 must wear a motorcycle helmet meeting FMVSS 218 on a highway
Must be street-legal (lights, mirrors and other motorcycle equipment), titled and registered with the Division of Motor Vehicles, and insured to ride on public roads
Barred from freeways, since §41-6a-1511 treats an electric motorcycle as a high power electric device
Off-road, one designed primarily for off-highway use is ridden as an off-highway motorcycle with OHV registration instead
From January 1, 2027, commercial sellers must disclose in sales and advertising that it is not an electric assisted bicycle but a motor vehicle subject to motor vehicle laws
Police are citing and impounding unregistered high-powered electric bikes ridden on public roads, sidewalks or paths
